answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Lapidary cut stone proof witnessed by the gem hall. It demands each cut stone is a decade of logged cut stones plus a signed guild record, so a farm must cut a hundred real stones by hand, and the horizon is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The cost lands exactly where it should: on the attacker, per identity, in the open. The opal is public, auditable, and impossible to discount in bulk. The kernel is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
